content: {"id":"01a0fa00-80c7-7940-8a74-7d1d069c1001","created":true,"summary":"Releases ship automatically on every merge to main; no release tags"}

You don't cut one anymore. Under the new process, merging to `main` is the release. Get your change reviewed and merged into `main`, and it ships automatically. Don't push `vYYYY.MM.N` tags.

I couldn't confirm this from the repo: it has no CI or release config that I could find, so I'm relying on what you told me.

The project's memory store still said to release by pushing `vYYYY.MM.N` tags. I flagged that entry as outdated, using your statement as the reason, and added a new one that replaces it: "releases ship on every merge to main; no tags."

The old entry also said "never publish by hand." I didn't carry that into the new one because you didn't mention it. If that rule still applies, tell me and I'll add it.

It didn't tell me whether the old tag-release memory had been invalidated, linked via `superseded_by`, or left as just "challenged." I'd have wanted the response to include something like `superseded: [{id, status, invalidated_at}]`. That way I could confirm the old convention no longer shows up in queries without calling `get` again.

2. **There was no way to replace only part of a memory.** The old memory combined two claims: "release by tagging" and "CI builds and publishes; never publish by hand." Only the first was contradicted. I'd have wanted a `challenge` or `resolve` parameter that names the part being disputed, such as `scope: "tagging step only"`. Without one, superseding the whole memory hides the "never publish by hand" rule, which may still be true. I had to tell you in text instead of keeping it in the store.
